speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help you, please tell me when these symptoms first started and if they came on suddenly or gradually.

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; given your age, diabetes, steroid use, and the progressive nature of your symptoms, I need to know if the weakness is confined strictly to the arm or if it has spread to your neck, shoulder, or trunk. Additionally, have you noticed any muscle wasting or atrophy in the right arm compared to the left?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, and Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone. REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study_and_Electromyography (EMG) of the right arm. Have you noticed any visible shrinking of the muscles in your right arm, such as a loss of bulk in your forearm or hand?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Brachial Plexopathy (likely Neoplastic or Traumatic).

Given the patient's history of anabolic steroid use, unexplained weight loss, and the specific combination of progressive weakness, sensory loss, and pain in a single limb, I am requesting images to look for a mass lesion or structural damage.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brachial_Plexus.

Please describe the results of the nerve conduction study once they are available, and confirm if there is visible muscle atrophy in the right arm.
